task.description: You are on branch feature/WF03-ISS0392-20260901 (checkout/pull it first). SECURITY-REVIEWER already PASSED this diff (git diff main...HEAD -- lib/, entirely lib/letflow/engine.ex, commit e30873f8). Run your idiom/scope gate against the same diff: ELIXIR-DEV's fix for ISS-0392 (Ecto.Multi :task_records key collision when a SUB_PROCESS child completes synchronously). Check the four standard questions -- idiomatic vs. crutch, supervision integrity (N/A here, no gen_statem/supervisor code touched -- confirm that's actually true), type-safety gaps (is a skip_task_activation? :: boolean() control-flow flag the right shape, or does it invite a future caller to misuse it -- flag if worth a type-safety issue, doesn't block PASS), and scope creep (does the new private helper maybe_append_task_activation_multi/7 add appropriately-scoped machinery for this fix, or does it over-engineer beyond what ISS-0392 needs). Also verify: the fix is documented well enough that a future reader understands WHY the conditional exists (not just that it does) -- check for a comment/moduledoc note explaining the collision this prevents, since a bare boolean-gated call site with no explanation is exactly the kind of silent workaround this pipeline's own history (see docs/anti-patterns.md) has flagged before when undocumented. SECURITY-REVIEWER also filed a MINOR finding (see step-03b-security-reviewer.json's result.issues) about a second, distinct, pre-existing Multi-collision class (two-or-more concurrent synchronously-completing SUB_PROCESS children in the same hop chain via a PARALLEL_GATEWAY) that this fix does not address -- confirm you agree it's out of scope for ISS-0392 specifically (a genuinely different collision than the one filed) rather than something this diff should have covered.
acceptance_criteria: Idiomatic-vs-crutch, supervision, type-safety, and scope-creep questions all explicitly addressed
Confirms whether the fix's rationale (why the conditional skip is safe) is documented in code comments, not only in the design doc/handoffs -- flag if missing
Independently agrees or disagrees with SECURITY-REVIEWER's characterization of the second collision class as out-of-scope pre-existing, with reasoning
No scope creep beyond what ISS-0392 requires
Checked against docs/anti-patterns.md if it has relevant entries

result.summary:
Reviewed git diff main...HEAD -- lib/ (commit e30873f8, entirely lib/letflow/engine.ex, 73 lines +/-3): build_complete_task_tail_multi/6's second clause gains a locally-computed skip_task_activation? predicate; build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3 -> /4 gains that boolean parameter; a new private helper maybe_append_task_activation_multi/7 (two total, exhaustive clauses on true/false) dispatches on it.

1. IDIOMATIC VS. CRUTCH -- PASS. This is plain-Elixir control flow gating whether an Ecto.Multi step is composed, not a hand-rolled state machine substituting for gen_statem, and not a boolean flag threaded to fake a case-do dispatch that OTP should own. maybe_append_task_activation_multi/7 is a textbook idiomatic use of multiple function-head pattern-matched clauses (true/false, exhaustive over boolean()) instead of an if/case body -- the idiomatic Elixir shape, not a crutch. No behaviour/protocol was warranted here and none was reached for.

2. SUPERVISION -- N/A, confirmed true rather than assumed. lib/letflow/engine.ex's own moduledoc (lines ~10, 225-230, 304-327) explicitly documents Letflow.Engine as a pure-function module operating under Ecto.Multi/Repo.transaction, NOT a supervised gen_statem/DynamicSupervisor-per-instance process -- per-instance process isolation lives in Letflow.InstanceSupervisor, a separate module untouched by this diff. Grepped the diff and confirming context for GenServer/gen_statem/Supervisor usage: zero hits in the changed hunks. No isolation boundary collapsed; nothing to check here beyond confirming the premise, which holds.

3. TYPE-SAFETY GAPS -- checked, does not block PASS, no new issue filed. skip_task_activation? :: boolean() is derived via Enum.any?/2 directly from prepared.child_initial_state.status, which is ALREADY a proper 4-value @type status :: :active | :completed | :cancelled | :error (lib/letflow/engine/instance_state.ex:68), Ecto.Enum-compatible by the module's own design note. The boolean isn't hiding an unrepresentable-state problem -- it's a derived summary ("does at least one child match :completed") of an already-typed field, computed and consumed entirely within one function's body (never stored, never passed across a process/API boundary, never a caller-supplied argument that could be misused). maybe_append_task_activation_multi/7's two clauses are exhaustive over boolean(), so Dialyzer/the type system already rules out a third case. This is a genuinely local, well-typed predicate, not a stringly/loosely-typed control flag inviting misuse by a future caller -- no type-safety issue worth filing under docs/issues/.

4. SCOPE CREEP -- PASS, no creep. The diff is exactly what ISS-0392 and the Revision-2 design (lib/letflow/design/iss0392-multi-task-records-collision-fix.md §2.4-§2.5) call for: one new parameter, one new 7-arity private helper with two clauses, zero new abstractions (no behaviour, no macro, no generic plumbing), zero signature changes to any of the five other functions in the call chain (append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6, SubProcess.append_start_multi/7, maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6, append_completion_multi/5, build_completion_write_steps/12) that Revision 1's withdrawn accumulator-threading mechanism would have touched. maybe_append_task_activation_multi/7 is scoped to exactly the one call site that needs the conditional and does not attempt to generalize into a reusable 'conditional multi-step' utility ahead of any recorded need -- appropriately narrow for a single-issue fix.

5. RATIONALE DOCUMENTED IN CODE, NOT JUST DESIGN DOC/HANDOFFS -- CONFIRMED PRESENT, this is not a bare undocumented boolean-gated call site. Three separate comment blocks were added directly in engine.ex: (a) at the skip_task_activation? computation (engine.ex ~2415-2427) explaining which collision this prevents, citing design doc §2.2/§2.4 and naming the exact colliding call chain (SubProcess.maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6 -> append_completion_multi/5 -> build_completion_write_steps/12) and the dominance rationale (§2.3) for why call (1) is skipped rather than replaced; (b) at build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/4's def, citing §2.5 and stating the return-type-unchanged guarantee; (c) at maybe_append_task_activation_multi/7's def, restating which call site becomes sole appender and that the false-branch is byte-for-byte prior behavior. This is exactly the kind of in-code WHY-documentation this project's own docs/anti-patterns.md repeatedly flags as missing elsewhere (silent/undocumented-workaround entries throughout the file) -- ELIXIR-DEV got this right; nothing to send back on this criterion.

6. SECURITY-REVIEWER's MINOR finding (second, distinct collision class: 2+ prepared_children entries independently completing synchronously in the same hop chain, e.g. via a prior PARALLEL_GATEWAY split) -- INDEPENDENTLY ASSESSED, AGREE it is out of scope for ISS-0392 specifically. Reasoning, verified against the actual code rather than taking either prior report at face value: ISS-0392's filed repro (docs/issues/ISS-0392.yaml) and the design doc's own root-cause recap (§1) both describe exactly ONE collision shape -- call (1) (build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi, the parent hop chain's own task-activation step) vs. call (2) (a single synchronously-completing child's cascade). skip_task_activation? is a predicate over 'does ANY prepared_children entry complete synchronously' and its only effect is to omit call (1) when that's true -- it says nothing about, and has no mechanism to prevent, two or more call (2)-shaped cascades from EACH independently trying to append {:task_records, parent_instance_id} for the SAME key. That is a call(2)-vs-call(2) collision, structurally distinct from call(1)-vs-call(2), living entirely inside append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6's Enum.reduce over prepared_children (engine.ex:2502-2521, itself unchanged by this diff) and sub_process.ex's build_completion_write_steps/12 (also confirmed zero-diff via git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex). Confirming SECURITY-REVIEWER's own claim that sub_process.ex has zero diff: verified independently, empty output. The fix's own design doc never claims to address multiple-simultaneous-synchronous-children (its §3's scope is the grandparent-cascade case/OQ-2, a different edge case again) -- so this is a real, pre-existing, unaddressed gap correctly characterized as out-of-scope for THIS diff, not something this diff should have covered. It should be filed as its own issue (as SECURITY-REVIEWER already recommended) rather than block this PASS.

7. docs/anti-patterns.md CHECK -- no entry directly on point (searched for task_records/multi collision/boolean flag/silent-workaround patterns); the closest-in-spirit entries are about silent/undocumented workarounds generally, which this diff avoids per point 5 above. No new anti-pattern entry needed from this review -- ELIXIR-DEV's documentation practice here is exemplary, not a new mistake to record.

OVERALL: idiomatic, correctly scoped, well-documented, supervision N/A as claimed, no blocking type-safety gap. PASS.

ORCH should separately file SECURITY-REVIEWER's MINOR finding (call(2)-vs-call(2) multi-synchronous-child collision) as a new issue via ISSUE_QUEUE.md, distinct from ISS-0392 -- REVIEWER independently confirms this characterization is correct.
